chunks: And in the narration of al-Bazanti, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr.
He said: I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a muhrim who killed a fox.
He said: "A blood sacrifice is upon him." I said: "What about a rabbit?" He said: "The same as what is for the fox."

key_terms.ثَعْلَبًا: a fox, whose killing here incurs a legal penalty in ihram
key_terms.دَمٌ: a blood sacrifice, meaning an animal offering as expiation
key_terms.فَأَرْنَبًا: a rabbit; asked about here in comparison to the fox
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: a person in the state of ihram during hajj or ʿumrah
key_terms.مِثْلُ: the same ruling or equivalent obligation

ai.seo_question: What is required of a muhrim who kills a fox or a rabbit?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning hunting while in the state of ihram. It states that killing a fox requires a blood sacrifice, and that the ruling for killing a rabbit is the same.
